title: Proactive priming, tenant soft-preemption and telemetry for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Maya Chen
description: After the hosted API GPU exhaustion incident on 2025-02-07 we observed systemic queue buildup and prolonged throttling for medium-priority tenants. This ticket implements a combined approach: (1) predictive pool priming (pre-warm) using short-window demand forecasts to reduce cold-start queue amplification, (2) tenant soft-preemption to gracefully shed non-critical in-flight prefetches and batch windows under sustained pressure, and (3) expanded telemetry (new SLO-aligned signals and tenant-level backpressure traces) to validate effectiveness and tune policies. Goals: reduce tail queue length by >=50% during spikes, keep P99 latency regression <5% compared to baseline, and provide clear per-tenant signalging for oncall playbooks.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Kickoff: Reviewed postmortem notes (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted-gpu-exhaustion-20250207). Agreed on three workstreams: forecasting model, pre-warm orchestration, and soft-preempt admission policy. Assigned leads: Luis (pre-warm + admission), Priya (telemetry), Dan (autoscaler hooks).

2025-02-24 - Telemetry spike: Added new 'queue_age_histogram' and 'tenant_prefetch_count' metrics to hosted-api-prod prom endpoint. Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/gpu-prime-v2. Initial capture shows prefetch-heavy tenants correlate with >70% of KV cache churn during bursts.

2025-02-27 - Design decision: Prefer short, jittered predictive primes (10-30s horizon) over long pre-warm windows to avoid cold-cache amplification and unnecessary cost. Trade-off: shorter primes reduce wasted cycles but require higher forecast accuracy; we will bootstrap with simple EWMA demand estimators and iterate.
2025-02-28 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/priming-orchestrator/pull/42 - implements priming controller and dry-run mode. Requesting review from @karen and @sahil.

2025-03-01 - Soft-preempt proposal reviewed in eng sync: policy will target prefetch and background batching only; do NOT preempt active user foreground requests. Preempted work will be marked with tenant-scope grace tokens to allow retries. Edge-case: long-running streaming sessions will be exempt. Decision recorded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/soft-preempt-policy.

2025-03-02 - Telemetry validation: initial AB test (canary) of predictive priming on 5 pilot pools. Early signals: 22% reduction in queue depth during the simulated spike test, latency P95 unchanged, P99 down 6% for pilot tenants. Action: proceed to widen canary and enable soft-preempt in dry-run mode.

Follow-ups: (a) integrate priming signals into autoscaler priming budget (ENG-273111 planned), (b) add tenant-level backpressure tracing to the trace headers (PR linked in the above priming PR), (c) schedule runbook update for oncall including new Grafana panels and recommended mitigation steps.
Blocked items: Need SRE approval for autoscaler permission changes to allow priming controller to allocate short-lived priming capacity. Raised ENG-811214 as permission request (pending).
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to non-invasive controls (observability + soft preemption + short priming) so we can iterate quickly without major infra churn. If metrics are promising we will follow with a second ticket to integrate learned thresholds into the main autoscaler and billing knobs. Also coordinate with solutions engineering for customers on Dedicated who may want similar pre-warm controls.
